transcript.description: One complete whole-model request between the real JavaScript requester (server/whole-model-requester.js over the mesh and the swarm transport) and the real provider protocol code, in one process, with fixed keys, clock, nonces and salt. frames are the data-channel messages in the order they were sent; the text of each message is the JSON text of envelope with its members in the order shown and no white space. A requester that receives the provider frames in this order and uses the fixed inputs can reproduce every requester frame byte for byte.

codeCases.name: wrong-code
codeCases.description: A well-formed code the desktop never issued. The desktop answers nothing. The real code still works afterwards.

codeCases.name: expired-code
codeCases.description: The right code, used at the moment it expires (issued.expiresAt). The desktop answers nothing and its owner is not asked.

codeCases.name: replayed-code
codeCases.description: The right code, used again after it paired the phone. The desktop answers nothing; its owner was asked once.

codeCases.name: declined
codeCases.description: The desktop owner answers no. The phone stores nothing, and the same code gets no answer afterwards.

codeCases.name: wrong-desktop
codeCases.description: The link names a desktop identity that no connection in the room proves to be. The phone never sends the code.

error.message: Could not find the verified desktop on this connection. Confirm it is online and retry.
error.name: Error

recognition.name: new-connection-name
recognition.description: After pairing, the desktop and the phone reconnect under new connection names and certificates. The phone finds the desktop by its proven identity and the named-recipient request is answered.

messages.content: What is the capital of France?

recognition.name: look-alike
recognition.description: The room holds another desktop with another key whose advertisement claims the paired desktop's id, serving the same model. The phone reports its desktop offline and sends the look-alike nothing, although the public catalog rule shows the model ready.

recognition.name: desktop-forgot
recognition.description: The desktop's pairing state was deleted (the only way the current code drops a phone). The phone still recognises the desktop, and its request is refused before the prompt.
